speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. Can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is it green or bilious?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby had any episodes of passing gas or stool that contained blood or mucus, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease.

Given the history of abdominal distension, feeding difficulty, and pain on palpation without signs of acute infection or obstruction like bilious vomiting, I suspect a congenital motility issue. I will request an abdominal X-ray to confirm the presence of gas patterns or meconium ileus equivalent before proceeding.
